mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the prior three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of quarters where this trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of such triggers, or the median return is not statistically negative at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which increases input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and persistent decline in both CPIAUCSL (inflation) and FEDFUNDS over three months indicates a deflationary policy stance, which increases real discount rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS both fall for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such joint declines, or the median return is not significantly negative at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A strong and sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such episodes, or the median return is not significantly positive at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE over two months indicates robust labor market expansion, which increases consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such joint increases, or the median return is not significantly positive at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent and broad-based increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) over four consecutive months, without a corresponding rise in consumption (GDPC1), signals a savings glut that reduces near-term demand for goods and services, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises for four consecutive months while GDPC1 does not
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes, or the median return is not significantly negative at 95% confidence.
